title: Deactivate authenticator app
purpose: Remove the app-based second factor from your account.
summary: Remove the authenticator app from your account, so sign-in no longer asks for its code.

tasks.title: Remove the authenticator app
steps: Select [[Deactivate]]. You return to Two-factor authentication.

tasks.title: Keep the app
steps: Leave with the normal account navigation without selecting Deactivate.

good_to_know: Your recovery codes are deleted too when no other authenticator remains.
Removing the app does not change your password or laboratory roles.
You may be asked to confirm your password or a code first.
If your laboratory requires a second factor of your account, you set up a new app before you can go on.
Where your laboratory sends email, you get an email when you do this, so you would notice if someone else did.

items.label: Deactivate
items.description: POSTs removal of the signed-in account’s TOTP authenticator after recent reauthentication. If no other non-recovery authenticator remains, recovery codes are deleted as well. Returns to the MFA overview. Where the deployment sends email, the account's email address gets a notice of the change, whatever was chosen on Email notices, and the change is recorded in the audit history (ids, type and times only). The notice says the app was removed, with its recovery codes when they go too.

sections.title: Eligibility and navigation
paragraphs: Requires an existing TOTP record, sign-in and recent reauthentication, normally within five minutes. This form has no editable fields, Back button or Cancel button. Leave via normal account navigation without submitting to keep the app active. Removing TOTP here does not remove laboratory roles or change the password. The normal flow performs recovery-code cleanup; direct maintenance deletion has different behavior.

Removing the app is always allowed. Every session of your account that the laboratory's second sign-in factor rule covered as it signed in, this one and any other, is sent to Set up a second sign-in factor at its next request while the rule still covers your account, and opens nothing else until a new app is active. Sessions the rule did not cover at sign-in are held to it from their next sign-in.
